questions.question: Explain what mutually exclusive and exhaustive mean for the options of a tick-one question.
questions.expected_answer: Mutually exclusive means no respondent can honestly tick two options, so categories must not overlap. Exhaustive means every respondent can honestly tick one option, so there must be no gaps, including never, nothing or other where they could apply, and an open top interval for numbers.

questions.question: Why is do you buy from the tuck shop and would you buy fruit a poor question?
questions.expected_answer: It is double-barrelled: two questions share one yes or no, which cannot represent the four possible combinations of answers. It hides the learners who do not buy now but would buy fruit. Split it into two separate questions.

questions.question: What is a pilot and why is it worth the time?
questions.expected_answer: A pilot is a trial of the questionnaire on a few people like the sample before the real survey. Watching them reveals hesitation, double ticks and skipped questions, which point to unclear wording, overlaps and gaps. Faults found after the forms are collected cannot be fixed.
